As the days grow shorter, heading outdoors can feel harder. But gathering with others in the daylight among the trees and the water is a grounding practice that can help us live through the cooler season with intention. Take a break from life s pressures and join us for this late fall walk at the beautiful Wapato Park. We will listen to the trees, pay attention to the many native plants around us, breathe in together and reflect by the lake.

Make sure to check the forecast. Bring layers, comfortable shoes, water, and anything else you need to be comfortable. We hold our walks rain or shine. If in doubt, please check our social media and website calendar for updates.

This walk will be offered in Spanish and English thanks to our partner Claudia Linares from Girasol Counseling.

Cuando los días se hacen más cortos, se nos antoja menos salir de casa. Pero reunirnos con otra gente en el día, entre los árboles y cerca del agua, puede revitalizarnos en la temporada de frío y ayudarnos a vivir el invierno con más intención. Te invitamos a descansar de las presiones del día a día en esta caminata otoñal en el hermoso Wapato Park. Pondremos atención a lo que nos dicen los árboles y las plantas autóctonas que nos rodean. Respiraremos hondo y reflexionaremos juntes a la orilla del lago.

Consulta el clima antes de salir de casa. Te recomendamos usar capas, zapatos cómodos, y traer cualquier otra cosa que sea necesaria para que estés cómode durante nuestro tiempo juntos. Sólo cancelamos nuestras caminatas si el clima supone un riesgo para los asistentes. Si tienes dudas, consulta nuestro sitio web y medios sociales para confirmar el estatus del evento.

Esta caminata es una colaboración entre TTF, Strategic Nature, y Girasol Counseling.

description: Our next chapter at Tacoma Arts Live is about more than performances. Lecture 6 | Dale Chihuly

How Tacoma s own Chihuly brought Studio Glass into the global imagination, inspiring countless artists and redefining glass as large-scale public art.

In celebration of America s 250th anniversary in 2026, and in partnership with America 250, Forged in Fire at Museum of Glass will combine illustrated lectures, live glassblowing demonstrations, and multimedia content to trace the evolution of American glassmaking, from colonial Jamestown to the contemporary works of Dale Chihuly. Each event illuminates the artistry, design, and cultural significance of glass as both a decorative and functional medium. Forged in Fire will reach diverse audiences throughout the Puget Sound region and beyond via in-person events and live streams, and build community pride in the region s unique role in the American Studio Glass Movement — a movement co-founded by Tacoma-native Dale Chihuly. By combining history, artistry, and live craft, this program exemplifies how decorative arts can spark curiosity, fuel discovery, and create shared cultural experiences.

Lectures and Demonstrations

Museum of Glass will host six unique public sessions pairing glass history talks by renowned glass artist and historian Walter Lieberman with live demonstrations by the Museum s internationally acclaimed Hot Shop Team. Each lecture focuses on a specific period of time in glassmaking history and is accompanied by a demonstration that recreates period-specific objects and techniques, giving audiences tangible insight into the evolution of glass as a decorative art form. All lectures will take place on select Saturdays 1pm in the Museum of Glass Hot Shop. The glassmaking demonstrations will follow at 2pm.

The Kareem Kandi World Orchestra is a dynamic and innovative ensemble committed to providing high-quality performances and music education to communities worldwide. Through a blend of concerts, workshops, compositions, recordings, and cultural exchanges, the orchestra brings people together through the universal language of music, with a special emphasis on the rich traditions of jazz.

Led by saxophonist, composer, and educator Kareem Kandi, the orchestra draws on his vast experience as a performer who has earned acclaim for his work in jazz, blues, classical, and funk. A native of the Pacific Northwest, Kareems versatility as a saxophonist and composer has taken him across the U.S. and around the globe, captivating audiences and critics alike. Known for his ability to honor the traditions of the past while forging new creative pathways, Kareems compositions and unique arrangements of timeless American standards continue to push musical boundaries.

Since 1996, Kareem has performed as both a bandleader and sideman, sharing the stage with luminaries such as Patti Labelle, Ali Jackson, George Colligan, Pete Christlieb, Bill Watrous, The Seattle Symphony, The Paperboys, The Temptations, The Four Tops, and many more. His work with The Kareem Kandi World Orchestra featuring embodies a sound that is fresh, innovative, and appeals to a diverse range of audiences. Each member brings decades of experience and mastery of their instruments, contributing to a performance that transcends genres and connects with listeners on many levels.

About Ali Jackson:

Ali Jackson has performed and recorded with a multitude of artists including Wynton Marsalis, Jon Batiste, Willie Nelson, Tony Bennett, Faith Hill, Karriem Riggins, Bobby McFerrin, Buster Williams, Norah Jones, Eric Clapton, Dee Dee Bridgewater, Aretha Franklin, George Benson, Harry Connick, Jr., KRS-1, Marcus Roberts, Joshua Redman, Vinx, Seito Kinen, Seiji Ozawa, Diana Krall, Gerald Albright, Michael Heise, Russell Gunn, James Morrison, Craig Handy, Jacky Terrasson, Kurt Rosenwinkel, and the New York City Ballet.

As a bandleader, Ali has recorded five albums, including Amalgamations, Wheelz Keep Rollin , Big Brown Getdown and the Yes! Trio album. Ali s playing is featured on more than 40 other albums, including Congo Square, Touchdown, Gunn Fu, Young Gunn Plus, European Sessions, Live at Yoshi s, Reflections in Change, Back East, Two Men With The Blues, Three-Five, Here We Go Again: Celebrating the Genius of Ray Charles, He and She, The Magic Hour and From the Plantation to the Penitentiary. Jackson also collaborated with jazz greats Cyrus Chestnut, Reginald Veal, and James

Carter on Gold Sounds, an innovative album that sought to transform songs by indie alternative rock band Pavement into unique virtuosic interpretations with the spirit of the church and the attitude of the juke joint. His production skills can be heard on George Benson s album Irreplaceable. He is also the voice of Duck Ellington, a character in the Penguin book series Baby Loves Jazz.

Ali is also an acclaimed composer whose voice is unique in its command of the universal language of the groove and the power of thoughtful use of space — both rhythmically and harmonically. His most recent masterworks include the Jazz at Lincoln Center Orchestra-commissioned Living Grooves: A World in Jazz Rhythm and a ballet composed for the Alvin Ailey Dance Company titled r-Evolution, Dream.

Ali s collaborations with other artists continue to push the envelope of jazz music and its connection to the human spirit. In 2010, Ali executive produced an original work called Beats of NYC, a project blending the musical idioms of Congolese, Senegalese, Tap, and modern dances juxtaposed with various styles of spoken word and the history of the blues. He also composed a ballet with long-time collaborator Hope Boykin titled Ballet: Watching go by the Day.

Junior Community Scientists

Ever wondered what it s like to participate in community science projects? Join Communities for a Healthy Bay for a hands-on half-day adventure exploring Commencement Bay from the water and the shore!

Youth will depart from the CHB office aboard our boat for a bay patrol, stopping along the way to conduct real water quality testing and help record water color data for ongoing monitoring efforts. Next, they ll get up close with the bay s smallest residents during a plankton sampling session, using nets and microscopes to see what s living beneath the surface.
The adventure continues at Owen Beach, where kids will join in a Green Crab Molt Search — helping track this invasive species by combing the shoreline for shed crab shells — before refueling with a provided lunch by the water. Then it s back aboard for the cruise home to the CHB office.

Kids will leave with real hands-on science experience, a better understanding of the bay they call home, and a taste of what it means to protect it.

This program is FREE! Lunch is provided.

description: Join us for the official record release show for IROIRO s self-titled debut full-length, out on K Records/Grand Ultra, at The Eleanor Room. Select Level will be opening the night. About IROIRO It only took a few gigs for IROIRO to establish themselves as Seattle s most exciting rock group. This may surprise fans of IQU, whose Michiko Swiggs and Kento Oiwa form IROIRO s creative core. Whereas IQU combined samples and live instrumentation to put playful spins on electronic music, IROIRO produce extended, vocal-free jams that blossom into powerful psychedelic rock. You can hear the band s splendid evolution on their self-titled debut LP. In the aftermath of early- 20s IQU reunion gigs and the disbanding of synthesist Swiggs and drummer Justin Schwartz s electronic unit Zazaz, they asked Oiwa to join them in a new project. Kento—who d been involved in solo improv project Malaise—agreed. Along with newly added bassist James Drage, they assembled for jam sessions at which the trio combined Zazaz s man-machine methods and Malaise s spontaneous noise excursions. The resulting music will convince you that rock still has ingenuity to burn. About Select Level Heads may know Select Level mastermind Andy Sells best as the limber drummer for soulful fusion explorers Afrocop or as the bassist for noisy prog-rockers Nosretep… or maybe even for his stint in electronic brainiacs FCS North, who existed from 1997 to 2007. This talented Seattle multi-instrumentalist has established that he can get weird and far out in various situations. Select Level finds Sells veering off on a tangent into the realm of sleek music geared for dancing and romancing. Andy is joined by Noel Brass Jr. (Afrocop) on keys and Morgan Dixon (Spesh) on drums. title: Live at the Eleanor with Jazz Therapy
description: Jazz Therapy : This Christmas A Soulful Jazz Celebration – Featuring the music of This Christmas, plus soulful songs and gospel selections — Donny Hathaway, Stevie Wonder, The Carpenters, and The Preacher s Wife. THE BAND Teal Warren – Bass Pete Yankeh – Drums Henry Nielsen – Piano Bill Throssell – Trumpet & Flugel Horn Jon Fotheringill – Alto & Tenor Saxophone SPECIAL GUEST VOCALISTS Alma Villegas Cathy Satava In the vibrant tapestry of sound, where rhythm meets soul, Jazz Therapy emerges as a powerful force of musical healing. Born from the depths of rich jazz tradition and a passion for emotional expression, this dynamic ensemble brings an unparalleled fusion of soulful melodies, intricate rhythms, and exuberant improvisation that captivate audiences of all ages. Leader and visionary Teal Warren, renowned for his mastery of the bass and a deep-rooted passion for jazz as both a musician and army veteran, guides Jazz Therapy with an intuitive sense of harmony and collaboration. Drawing inspiration from many jazz legends, the ensemble creates a sonic universe where each note resonates with vibrant energy, inviting listeners to not only hear but to feel the music s transformative power. Collaborating with a talented lineup of seasoned musicians, Jazz Therapy is about more than just music—it s an experience. From the pulsing beats of slap bass to the gentle caress of a saxophone solo, every performance is a journey that fosters connection, reflection, and empowerment. This sense of unity is the bedrock of the band s philosophy, which centers on music as an innovative therapy — a sanctuary where individuals can come together, heal, and grow. With accolades that span esteemed jazz festivals and high-profile events, Jazz Therapy s eclectic repertoire seamlessly weaves in influences from modern jazz, blues, and world music, crafting a sound that s both a nod to the classics and a fresh auditory exploration. Each performance is an opportunity to not only entertain but to touch hearts and ignite spirits with the transformative magic of jazz. Jazz Therapy invites you to dive into their world, where music is the remedy and every performance is a soulful recollection of the universal language that binds us all. Whether you are a jazz connoisseur or a curious soul seeking refuge through sound, Jazz Therapy is exceptional, unforgettable, and ready to heal. Live at The Eleanor offers a cozy candlelit lounge experience where each performance unfolds like a conversation between artist and audience. Full bar and concessions are available; all ages are welcome.

Gretchen pursued both performance and music education at University of Washington, embracing an interwoven path of teaching and performing. T-Town Sensory Social Story The Tacoma Dome is a KultureCity Certified Sensory Inclusive Venue. That means that our staff has taken KultureCity Sensory Inclusion 101 so our venue can be more welcoming and accommodating to guests with sensory needs, not just during Sensory Hour times, but during all events. What is Sensory Hour? This time lets guests experience T-Town with lower sensory input to create a less overwhelming environment. Who is sensory hour for? Anyone with sensory sensitivities who would prefer a quieter, low-key exploration of T-Town. This includes individuals with autism, military vets with PTSD, adults with dementia, Parkinsons disease, stroke patients just to name a few. How does sensory hour work? During this time, we will: Dim overhead lighting Speak in quieter voices Turn off flashing lights on trucks Keep sirens and horns silent Play calm music quietly What if a guest has sensory needs and comes outside of the sensory hour time? KultureCity sensory bags and weighted lap pads are available for guests to borrow at the Guest Services Desk in the arena. Each sensory bag includes a KultureCity VIP lanyard, noise-reducing headphones, fidget tools, and a communication card. Guests who need a break from the event environment are also welcome to use the designated sensory-friendly nook at the Tacoma Venues & Events (TVE) booth. Questions? title: Walk for Reconciliation Against Racism 2026
description: The Chinese Reconciliation Project Foundation invites the public to join them and the Washington State Historical Museum at the 2026 Walk for Reconciliation Against Racism. This annual demonstration r…
big_desc:
The Chinese Reconciliation Project Foundation invites the public to join them and the Washington State Historical Museum at the 2026 Walk for Reconciliation Against Racism. This annual demonstration retraces and reverses the walking path of expulsion forced on Tacomas Chinese American population in 1885, reclaiming the City for all peoples and cultures.

The walk, led by civic, educational, business and faith leaders, will begin near Union Station, where the Chinese pioneers in 1885 were marched at gunpoint out of town. Walkers will proceed north, led by Chinese Lion Dancers, through downtown Tacoma where many Chinese, and later Japanese businesses and houses once stood, along Schuster Parkway and the railroad- largely built by Chinese labor, and finally arrive at the Chinese Reconciliation Park. Throughout the walk, attendees will be within a half mile of the Northwest ICE Processing Center (NWIPC) where a similar white nationalist agenda continues to be orchestrated.

This year, the Opening Ceremony will take place inside the Washington State History Museums Mt. Tahoma Auditorium at 10 AM. After brief remarks from our Emcee and guest speaker, the Walk will begin from outside the Union Station around 10:45 AM. Walkers will arrive at the Chinese Reconciliation Park by 12 PM, and the event will conclude with final remarks, performances, and refreshments. To learn more about our guest speakers and our events timing, please visit our website.

Event Timing

  • Welcome Speeches begin at 10 AM, in the Washington State History Museum s Mt. Tahoma Auditorium.
  • The walk begins at 11 AM, from the History Museum s auditorium to the Tacoma Chinese Reconciliation Park.
  • The Conclusion Ceremony begins at 12:30 PM, at the Tacoma Chinese Reconciliation Park, featuring remarks from local dignitaries, a performance, and refreshments.

This event is free, open to all and families and children are most welcome. Join us in solidarity on Saturday, October 24th as we commit ourselves to anti-racism in the City of Destiny

Bus Schedule

To ensure our Walk for Reconciliation Against Racism is inclusive and accessible to all, we have organized a bus to transport participants who are unable to walk the three mile distance from the Union Station to the Tacoma Chinese Reconciliation Park.

  • The bus leaves the Union Station area at 10:45 AM, to transport attendees to the Chinese Reconciliation Park
  • The bus back leaves the Chinese Reconciliation Park at 1:15 PM, bringing attendees back to the Union Station.

History of The Tacoma Method

November 3, 2026, is the 141st anniversary of the 1885 expulsion of all remaining Chinese residents of Tacoma (possibly as many as 200 people). Many Chinese had left earlier that fall because of the hostile atmosphere here in Tacoma. The Chinese Must Go campaign was not an official act of the City government, but it was openly instigated and organized by elected officials (including the mayor and members of the City Council) and other leading citizens of civic influence. Soon after the event, the expulsion became known as the Tacoma Method in a rising tide of anti-Chinese sentiment and acts of violence in the western United States.

Join us in solidarity on Saturday, October 24th as we commit ourselves to anti-racism in the City of Destiny.

For more information, visit crpftacoma.org or contact Ben Everett at info@crpftacoma.org.
